question.text: A current ' $I^{\prime}$ is flowing along an infinite, straight wire, in the positive $Z$ -direction and the same current is flowing along a similar parallel wire $5 \mathrm{m}$ apart, in the negative Z-direction. A point $P$ is at a perpendicular distance $3 \mathrm{m}$ from the first wire and $4 \mathrm{m}$ from the second. What will be magnitude of the magnetic field B of $P ?$

solution.text: According to the question. Magnetic field due to first wire $(A)$ is $B_{1}=\frac{\mu_{0} \times I}{2 \pi \times 3}$ Magnetic field due to second wire $(B)$ is $B_{2}=\frac{\mu_{0} \times 1}{2 \pi \times 4}$ Net magnitude of magnetic field $B=\sqrt{B_{1}^{2}+B_{2}^{2}}$ $$ B=\frac{\mu_{0} I}{2 \pi} \sqrt{\frac{1}{9}+\frac{1}{16}}=\frac{\mu_{0} I \times 5}{2 \pi \times 3 \times 4} $$ Magnetic field $B=\frac{5}{24} \times \frac{\mu_{0} I}{\pi}$
